page: Amazon Web Services r8g.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance type based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. The server is driven by AWS Neoverse-V2 processors utilizing the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. The configuration supplies 4 dedicated physical cores mapped to 4 vCPUs without multithreading, clocked at 2.8 GHz. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor subsystem integrates 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for standard AES encryption.

Hardware bundling is minimal, as the r8g.xlarge provides zero local storage and no integrated GPUs. All disk storage operations must be directed to external block storage volumes. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and the server allocation includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong performance in memory throughput and decompression, marked by a PassMark memory score of 2901.95 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 14.39 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 108.05 GB/sec. Core compute scores fall into the average range, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1861.0, multi-core score of 5724.0, and 8.53 million Redis SET operations per second. In contrast, PassMark CPU and cryptographic scores register in lower percentiles, and LLM text generation remains low at 6.5 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

The 8 GB per vCPU distribution offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-constrained workloads by preventing excess expenditure on compute cores. Primary operational fits include in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, relational databases, caching layers, and medium-scale data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with custom 64-bit Arm Neoverse-V2 processors. Operating at 2.8 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The processor incorporates 36 MB of L3 cache and native AES cryptography. The server contains no local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate strong memory subsystem throughput and decompression rates alongside solid Redis caching throughput at 8.53 million operations per second, though synthetic CPU extended instruction metrics remain comparatively weak. The hardware profile is balanced to maximize resource density for memory-bound tasks, making the instance well matched for in-memory databases, caching tiers, and general memory-intensive enterprise services.
